# nada


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

[Audio-JEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02915) on [Modular MAX](https://docs.modular.com/max/). This is the context encoder from `ltuncay/Audio-JEPA`: a ViT-Base that embeds a 10 s log-mel spectrogram as 128 tokens of width 768. The frontend is Kaldi fbank at 32 kHz. Predictor and target-encoder weights from the Lightning checkpoint are dropped; only `encoder.*` is used at inference.

The layout follows `solid_lens`. `config` is the architecture, `weights` binds a checkpoint, and [`compile_model`](https://alix559.github.io/nada/model.html#compile_model) traces the module for one batch size and one spectrogram size. The graph is a MAX module (`max.experimental.nn`): the same `forward` runs eagerly or compiled. Module and parameter names match the published encoder, so its state dict loads without renaming.

## Install

``` sh
pixi install
pixi run -e reference convert
```

[`convert`](https://alix559.github.io/nada/download.html#convert) downloads `JEPA.ckpt` from Hugging Face and writes `models/audio_jepa.safetensors`. The Lightning file needs PyTorch to read, so conversion runs in the `reference` environment.

## Embed

``` sh
pixi run embed clip.wav
```

The clip is 16-bit PCM WAV. 32 kHz is native; other rates are resampled. The same thing from Python:

``` python
from nada.features import read_wav
from nada.model import build, compile_model, load_checkpoint, embed

clip = read_wav("clip.wav")
model = build()
load_checkpoint(model)
compiled = compile_model(model, batch=1)
print(embed(model, compiled, [clip])[0].shape)
```

`compiled` takes a float32 spectrogram of shape `(batch, 256, 128, 1)` and returns patch tokens `(batch, 128, 768)`. `embed` mean-pools those tokens to one vector per clip. The graph is compiled for one spectrogram size; the pretrained model is always 256 × 128.

## Check

``` sh
pixi run smoke
pixi run -e reference parity
```

`smoke` compiles a two-layer ViT and checks that the tokens are finite and the right shape. `parity` compares the numpy Kaldi frontend with `torchaudio`, and the MAX encoder with a PyTorch ViT of the same weights. The real checkpoint is compared too once it is converted.
